problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[2,5]\times [0,5]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-25 \\ {x}^{2}-y-20\end{aligned}].
$$

Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts at ${x}_{0}=[5,\,0]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[5,\,5]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).

feedback.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[1,2]\times [0,1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+y-xy-3 \\ {x}^{2}-x+y-2\end{aligned}].
$$

Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts at ${x}_{0}=[1,\,0]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[2,\,1]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).

| ${x}_{2}≈[$ | {{field-1}} | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-2}} |  |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+y-xy-3) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+y-xy-3) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-x+y-2) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-x+y-2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x-y & 1-x \\ 2x-1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}2x-y & 1-x \\ 2x-1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+y-xy-3 \\ {x}^{2}-x+y-2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}2x-y & 1-x \\ 2x-1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+y-xy-3 \\ {x}^{2}-x+y-2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}2(2)-(1) & 1-(2) \\ 2(2)-1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}(2)^{2}+(1)-(2)(1)-3 \\ (2)^{2}-(2)+(1)-2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{3\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{11}{6} \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}1.833 \\ 0.5\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
